papers.title: RECONFIGURABLE ROBOTIC SWARMS AND CONTINUOUS FUNCTIONAL REGENERATION AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Works | White Rainbow Scientific Library | Flagship 02 Prospective Research Atlas — English Review Edition, October 2026 Can a distributed population of heterogeneous modular robots reconstruct an operationally qualified capability after damage, without treating a newly assembled shape as evidence of restored function? Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit develops an interdisciplinary research program on modular morphology, distributed self-assembly, task-dependent graph structure, mechanical qualification, connector fatigue, recoverable actions, and independent post-reconfiguration verification. Its central proposition is deliberately testable: a swarm may change its topology after losing modules, but it earns the stronger name of functional regeneration only when its restored configuration satisfies the original, independently assessed service requirements and does not conceal emerging hazards or latent joint failures. The monograph distinguishes three often conflated networks: mechanical connections that transmit forces, communication links that transmit information, and power connections that transport energy. It then investigates how graph connectivity, geometric rigidity, elastic stiffness, buckling, frictional contact, thermal dissipation, material fatigue, sensing uncertainty, local negotiation, and safe rollback constrain what an apparently repaired swarm can actually do. A prospective twenty-module testbed provides recurring engineering anchors: bridge, gripping, and sensing-tower tasks, blinded removal of modules, unseen configurations, independent qualification, and strong comparisons with redundant fixed structures and specialist replacement procedures. The research architecture includes thirty mathematically diverse derivation plates, eighty-two chapter-level questions and their five individually paginated study units, two hundred falsifiable Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. The companion spreadsheet links physical models, chapter topics, prospective study cards, provenance, source DOI records, and page references to support future research and AI-assisted scientific handoff. Published robotics literature supplies a source-grounded context for modular reconfigurable mechanisms and fault-aware planning, including external DOI records for reviews and an existing fault-tolerant modular system. The manuscript separates those precedents from its own unexecuted research designs. Its two STARLI mother volumes are listed as conceptual ancestry, not as independent experimental validation. Biological regeneration functions as an analogy for staged assessment of restoration, not as evidence of biomedical efficacy, autonomous human-tissue repair, or indefinite machine life. This is a prospective research-atlas REVIEW EDITION. The mathematical relations, study proposals, design seeds, and acceptance thresholds are not experimentally validated findings. External mathematical review, whole-text DOI auditing, and a stronger editorial review for chapter-level semantic repetition remain necessary before scholarly publication. Negative findings, conventional method superiority, irreversible module retirement, and scientific abstention are legitimate outcomes within this research program. STARLI | 33 | White Rainbow Scientific Library

papers.title: MICROROBOTIC BCI CO-DESIGN FOR STROKE REHABILITATION AT THE LIMIT Motor Intention x Minimal Local Assistance x Real Functional Recovery Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI | Research Atlas XXIII.13 | 2026 A nonclinical, falsifiable research monograph that asks whether an intention-confirming brain-computer interface (BCI) combined with carefully bounded local microrobotic assistance could improve genuinely unassisted upper-limb function after stroke. The central question is deliberately harder than predicting motor intent or completing a movement with a powered device: Does any gain survive withdrawal, transfer to novel activities, and outperform strong single-component comparators in blinded functional assessment? Across 82 distinct chapters and 410 one-section-per-page research units, the book separates residual voluntary capacity from device-mediated task completion; develops uncertainty-aware EEG/EMG intention tests; examines the mechanics, tracking, material accounting and safety challenges of actual microscale actuators; and derives assist-as-needed control strategies that can abstain, taper and stop. The design emphasizes a four-arm factorial decomposition, sham credibility, stage-specific stroke heterogeneity, clinically meaningful endpoint definitions, physiological-marker skepticism, transparent adverse-event governance and independent multi-center reproduction. Thirty substantial gold-ink mathematical derivation cards connect prespecified estimands, factorial interaction, calibration, magnetic and mechanical force, localized thermal bounds, motor-learning retention, missing-data sensitivity, safety feasibility and research value to later chapter arguments and experimental Gates. Two hundred independent Research Gates form detailed successor-ready cards specifying an adversarial question, comparator, measurement, falsifier and handoff record. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate solutions, including the Stroke Recovery Microcell. A source-role annotated DOI bibliography separates established BCI rehabilitation reports from still-speculative clinical translation of mobile medical microrobots. No device efficacy is asserted and no trial was performed for this monograph. Published BCI-robot stroke studies generally investigate external orthoses, exoskeletons or soft gloves; they do not establish that mobile microrobots in the nervous system restore function. No clinical treatment or device-use recommendation is provided. Independent safety vetoes for permission, irreversible harm, material recovery and raw-data integrity cannot be offset by a favorable weighted score. Architecture: research positioning and boundaries; five-layer system; reading guide; 30 linked mathematical derivations; 82 chapter introductions; five individual research sections per chapter; 200 Research Gates; conclusion, limitations and future roadmap; 17 external DOI literature entries; 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. The work is intended as a rigorous hypothesis library for future human and AI researchers, not a substitute for clinical evidence.

Reinforcement Learning Based Decision Support for Adaptive Pacing Control of Hand Activity Level
papers.summary: This paper presents a reinforcement learning based decision support system for adaptive pacing control in manual material handling tasks. Hand Activity Level optimization is formulated as a finite horizon Markov Decision Process, where actions select pacing intensities or micro breaks under stochastic object loads. Q-learning and Deep Q-learning are evaluated in simulation using productivity and cumulative ergonomic exposure metrics aligned with HAL-TLV guidelines. Results show that Deep Q-learning achieves higher productivity, but Q-learning has lower cumulative risk exposure.

papers.summary: This study investigates active wake control of a rectangular cylinder near a free surface using a mode-aware deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework aimed at reducing drag and suppressing vortex shedding. The flow is modeled as a two-dimensional incompressible two-phase system, with the air–water interface captured by the volume-of-fluid method. Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is first used to identify the region of strongest flow fluctuations, which is then encoded by a convolutional neural network into 12 latent signals as compact observations for the DRL agent.
